agent_value.text: All five transaction channels use the same VALID/READY handshake. Source generates VALID; destination generates READY. Transfer occurs only when both VALID and READY are HIGH at a rising edge of ACLK.
A source must not wait until READY is asserted before asserting VALID. Once VALID is asserted, it must remain asserted until the handshake occurs.
A destination is permitted to wait for VALID to be asserted before asserting READY. If READY is asserted, it is permitted to deassert READY before VALID is asserted.
On master and slave interfaces, there must be no combinatorial paths between input and output signals.
Each AXI interface has a single clock signal ACLK. All input signals are sampled on the rising edge of ACLK; all output signal changes can only occur after the rising edge of ACLK.
Reset signal ARESETn is active-LOW. Reset can be asserted asynchronously, but deassertion must be synchronous to ACLK.
During reset, master must drive ARVALID, AWVALID, WVALID LOW. Slave must drive RVALID and BVALID LOW. Earliest point a master may begin driving xVALID HIGH is the ACLK edge after ARESETn is HIGH.
Channel handshake dependency rule (anti-deadlock): The VALID of a sending interface must not be dependent on the READY of the receiving interface.
agent_value.source: A3.3.1 Dependencies between channel handshake signals

agent_value.text: Read dependency: slave must wait for both ARVALID and ARREADY to be asserted before asserting RVALID.
AXI3 write dependency: slave must wait for WVALID, WREADY, and WLAST before asserting BVALID.
AXI4/AXI5 additional write dependency: slave must wait for AWVALID, AWREADY, WVALID, and WREADY all asserted before asserting BVALID. The slave must also wait for WLAST before BVALID.
A write response must always follow the last write transfer in a write transaction.
Read data must always follow the read address of the data.
A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary.
For wrapping bursts, the burst length must be 2, 4, 8, or 16; start address must be aligned to the size of each transfer.
Early termination of bursts is not supported. To reduce data transferred in a write burst, the master may deassert all write strobes but must complete all transfers.
The master must assert WLAST while it is driving the final write transfer in the burst.
The slave must assert RLAST when it is driving the final read transfer in the burst.
When WVALID is LOW, the write strobes can take any value; spec recommends they are either driven LOW or held at their previous value.
Protocol requires that the required number of data transfers must be performed even if an error is reported. The remainder of the burst is not cancelled if the slave gives a single error response.
agent_value.source: A3.4.5 Read and write response structure

agent_value.text: For a write transaction, a single response is signaled for the entire burst, not for each data transfer.
In a read transaction, the slave can signal different responses for different transfers in a burst.
There is one write strobe for each 8 bits of the write data bus; WSTRB[n] corresponds to WDATA[(8n)+7:(8n)].
A master must issue write data in the same order that it issues the transaction addresses.
The interleaving of write data with different IDs was permitted in AXI3 but is deprecated in AXI4 and later.
When a master issues a write request, it must be able to provide all write data for that transaction without dependency on other transactions from that master.
When a master issues a read request, it must be able to accept all read data for that transaction without dependency on other transactions from that master.
All transactions with a given AXI ID value must remain in order; no restriction on ordering of transactions with different ID values.
The slave must ensure that the RID value of any returned data matches the ARID value of the address it is responding to.

The ordering model does not give any ordering guarantees between: transactions from different masters; read and write transactions; transactions with different IDs; transactions to different Peripheral regions; transactions to different Memory locations.
In AXI4, all Device transactions using the same ID to the same slave must be ordered with respect to each other.
Slave must also wait for WLAST to be asserted before asserting BVALID, because BRESP must be signaled only after the last data transfer of a write transaction.

agent_value: Master issues an exclusive read with some ARID at address X.
Slave that supports exclusive monitors X for that ARID.

encoding.name: 128B
encoding.semantics: 128 bytes per transfer. The size of any transfer must not exceed the data bus width of either agent.

encoding.name: FIXED
encoding.semantics: Address is the same for every transfer in the burst; valid byte lanes constant. Used for repeated accesses to the same location, e.g. FIFO load/empty.

encoding.name: INCR
encoding.semantics: Incrementing — address for each transfer in the burst is an increment of the previous address. Increment value depends on AxSIZE. Used for accesses to normal sequential memory.

encoding.name: WRAP
encoding.semantics: Wrapping — like INCR, but address wraps around to a lower address (the wrap boundary) when an upper limit is reached. Start address must be aligned to AxSIZE; burst length must be 2, 4, 8, or 16. Used for cache line accesses.

encoding.name: OKAY
encoding.semantics: Normal access success; or failure of an exclusive access; or exclusive access to a slave that does not support exclusive access. Default response.

encoding.name: EXOKAY
encoding.semantics: Exclusive access okay — success of an exclusive read or write. Only legal as a response to an exclusive transaction.

encoding.name: SLVERR
encoding.semantics: Slave error — access reached the slave successfully but the slave returns an error (e.g. FIFO overrun/underrun, unsupported size, write to read-only, slave timeout, access to disabled function).

encoding.name: DECERR
encoding.semantics: Decode error — typically generated by an interconnect to indicate that there is no slave at the transaction address. The interconnect should route to a default slave that returns DECERR.

encoding.name: Exclusive access
encoding.semantics: Exclusive access — selects exclusive read/write monitoring.

encoding.name: Locked access
encoding.semantics: Locked access — interconnect must ensure only this master can access the targeted slave region until an unlocked transaction from the same master completes. Removed in AXI4.

encoding.name: Exclusive access
encoding.semantics: Exclusive access — selects exclusive read/write monitoring. Locked access is removed in AXI4.

encoding.name: Non-bufferable
encoding.semantics: Bufferable (B) bit deasserted — transaction must NOT be delayed by the interconnect.

encoding.name: Bufferable
encoding.semantics: Bufferable (B) bit asserted — interconnect or any component can delay the transaction reaching its final destination for any number of cycles. Normally only relevant to writes.

encoding.name: Non-cacheable
encoding.semantics: Cacheable (C) bit deasserted — allocation of the transaction is forbidden.

encoding.name: Cacheable
encoding.semantics: Cacheable (C) bit asserted — allocation permitted; characteristics at final destination need not match the original.

encoding.name: Read-Allocate
encoding.semantics: RA bit asserted — must not be set if C bit deasserted.

encoding.name: Write-Allocate
encoding.semantics: WA bit asserted — must not be set if C bit deasserted.

encoding.name: Allocate
encoding.semantics: When asserted, transaction must be looked up in cache (could have been previously allocated); recommended to be allocated. When deasserted (and [2] deasserted), no lookup required, must propagate to final destination.

encoding.name: Other Allocate
encoding.semantics: When asserted, transaction must be looked up in cache (could have been allocated by another transaction/master). When deasserted (and [3] deasserted), no lookup required.

encoding.name: Modifiable
encoding.semantics: When asserted, transaction characteristics can be modified and writes can be merged. When deasserted, characteristics must not be modified.

encoding.name: Bufferable
encoding.semantics: When deasserted with [3:2] deasserted, write response must come from final destination. When asserted with [3:2] deasserted, response can come from intermediate point but write must be made visible at final destination in a timely manner. With [3:2] asserted, response can come from intermediate point.

encoding.name: Other Allocate
encoding.semantics: When asserted, transaction must be looked up in cache (could have been allocated by a write transaction or another master). When deasserted (and [2] deasserted), no lookup required.

encoding.name: Allocate
encoding.semantics: When asserted, transaction must be looked up in cache (could have been allocated); recommended to be allocated.

encoding.name: Modifiable
encoding.semantics: When asserted, characteristics can be modified and a larger quantity of read data can be fetched than required.

encoding.name: Bufferable
encoding.semantics: No effect if [3:1] deasserted. With [3:2] deasserted and [1] asserted: deasserted -> read data must come from final destination; asserted -> can come from final destination or a write progressing to it. When [3] or [2] asserted, distinguishes Write-Through vs Write-Back.

agent_value.name: AXI4 Memory type encoding (ARCACHE / AWCACHE -> memory type)

encoding.name: Device Non-bufferable
encoding.semantics: Write response from final destination; read data from final destination; Non-modifiable; no prefetch; no merging.

encoding.name: Device Bufferable
encoding.semantics: Write response can be intermediate; writes visible at final destination in a timely manner; reads from final destination; Non-modifiable; no prefetch; no merging.

encoding.name: Reserved
encoding.semantics: All values not shown in Table A4-5 are reserved.

encoding.name: Secure access
encoding.semantics: Secure address space (note: signal is asserted-LOW for Secure — bit value 0 == Secure).

encoding.name: Data access
encoding.semantics: Data access (recommended default unless instruction access is known).

encoding.name: Instruction access
encoding.semantics: Instruction access. AXI defines this as a hint; not accurate when a transaction contains a mix of instruction and data items.

encoding.name: Address
encoding.semantics: Must not be changed by interconnect when transaction is Non-modifiable.

encoding.name: Burst length
encoding.semantics: Must not be changed (AXI4 INCR>16 may be split, see A4.3).

encoding.name: WID (AXI3 only)
encoding.semantics: Write data channel ID; removed in AXI4.

encoding.name: BID
encoding.semantics: Write response channel ID — must match the AWID of the transaction being responded to.

encoding.name: RID
encoding.semantics: Read data channel ID — slave must ensure RID matches the ARID of the address it is responding to.

agent_value.sva_form: // Structural / synthesis lint rule; not expressible as a temporal SVA property.

agent_value.quote: During reset a master interface must drive ARVALID, AWVALID, and WVALID LOW. A slave interface must drive RVALID and BVALID LOW. The earliest point after reset that a master is permitted to begin driving ARVALID, AWVALID, or WVALID HIGH is at a rising ACLK edge after ARESETn is HIGH.

A source is not permitted to wait until READY is asserted before asserting VALID. When VALID is asserted, it must remain asserted until the handshake occurs, at a rising clock edge when VALID and READY are both asserted.
The VALID signal of the AXI interface sending information must not be dependent on the READY signal of the AXI interface receiving that information.
The slave must wait for both WVALID and WREADY to be asserted before asserting BVALID. The slave must also wait for WLAST to be asserted before asserting BVALID.

agent_value.spec_section: A3.3.1 AXI4 and AXI5 write transaction dependencies
agent_value.quote: The slave must wait for AWVALID, AWREADY, WVALID, and WREADY to be asserted before asserting BVALID.

AXI has the following rules governing the use of bursts: For wrapping bursts, the burst length must be 2, 4, 8, or 16. A burst must not cross a 4KB address boundary. Early termination of bursts is not supported.

The size of any transfer must not exceed the data bus width of either agent in the transaction. Burst type WRAP: the start address must be aligned to the size of each transfer; the length of the burst must be 2, 4, 8, or 16 transfers.

agent_value.spec_section: A3.4 Read and write response structure
agent_value.quote: For a write transaction, a single response is signaled for the entire burst, and not for each data transfer within the burst. The protocol specifies that the required number of data transfers must be performed, even if an error is reported.

The slave must ensure that the RID value of any returned data matches the ARID value of the address that it is responding to. A master must issue write data in the same order that it issues the transaction addresses.

A system is defined as being multi-copy atomic if writes to the same location are observed in the same order by all agents. It is required that the Multi_Copy_Atomicity property is True for Issue G and later of this specification.

The address of an exclusive access must be aligned to the total number of bytes in the transaction. The number of bytes to be transferred in an exclusive access burst must be a power of 2. The maximum number of bytes that can be transferred in an exclusive burst is 128. The burst length for an exclusive access must not exceed 16 transfers.
Mixing EXOKAY and OKAY responses in the same transaction is not permitted.

agent_value: Interconnect must realign the address and write data when determining the destination address space or slave space, so that write data is signaled as valid only to the slave it is destined for.

When a master is connected to an interconnect, the interconnect appends additional bits to the ARID, AWID and WID identifiers that are unique to that master port. Effects: (a) masters do not need to know what ID values other masters use; (b) ID identifier at the slave interface is wider than at the master interface.

For read data, the interconnect uses the additional bits of the RID identifier to determine which master port the read data is destined for, then removes these bits before passing RID to the master port.

For write response, the interconnect uses the additional bits of the BID identifier to determine which master port the response is destined for, then removes these bits before passing BID to the master port.
The interconnect must ensure that read data from a sequence of transactions with the same ARID targeting different slaves is received by the master in the order it issued the addresses.
An interconnect that combines write transactions from different masters must forward the write data in address order.
If the interconnect cannot successfully decode a slave access, it must return the DECERR response. Recommendation: route to a default slave that returns DECERR.
An AXI4 interconnect must preserve same-ID-same-slave ordering for Device (Non-modifiable) transactions; this is not an explicit requirement of AXI3.

AXI4 interconnect may convert INCR bursts with length >16 into multiple smaller bursts even if Non-modifiable. Generated bursts must retain the same transaction characteristics; only burst length is reduced and address adapted.

For locked transactions (AXI3 only), the interconnect must ensure that only the originating master can access the targeted slave region until an unlocked transaction from the same master completes; an arbiter within the interconnect must enforce this restriction.

In an AXI4 environment, the interconnect must convert any AXI3 locked transaction (AxLOCK[1:0]=0b10) into a normal transaction (AxLOCK=0b0); the conversion mechanism should optionally detect and flag that translation occurred.
Non-modifiable transaction parameters (AxADDR, AxSIZE, AxLEN, AxBURST, AxLOCK, AxCACHE, AxPROT) must not be changed by the interconnect when AxCACHE Modifiable bit is deasserted.
Each AXI interface has a single clock signal ACLK; an interconnect may include synchronous or asynchronous bridges between clock domains, but each interface itself is single-clock.
ARESETn may be asserted asynchronously, but deassertion must be synchronous with a rising edge of ACLK.
Interconnect must not introduce combinational paths from any READY signal back to the corresponding VALID signal.
The interconnect (when transforming Non-modifiable AXI4 INCR>16 into multiple smaller bursts) must generate bursts whose length is <=16 and whose start addresses are appropriately adapted.

agent_value.quote: Most systems use one of three interconnect topologies: shared address and data buses; shared address buses and multiple data buses; multilayer, with multiple address and data buses. agent_value.spec_section: A5.2.3 Interconnect use of transaction identifiers
agent_value.quote: When a master is connected to an interconnect, the interconnect appends additional bits to the ARID, AWID and WID identifiers that are unique to that master port. The ID identifier at a slave interface is wider than the ID identifier at a master interface. For read data, the interconnect uses the additional bits of the RID identifier to determine which master port the read data is destined for. The interconnect removes these bits of the RID identifier before passing the RID value to the correct master port.

The interconnect must ensure that the read data from a sequence of transactions with the same ARID value targeting different slaves is received by the master in the order that it issued the addresses.
An interconnect that combines write transactions from different masters must ensure that it forwards the write data in address order.

If the interconnect cannot successfully decode a slave access, it must return the DECERR response. This specification recommends that the interconnect routes the access to a default slave, and the default slave returns the DECERR response.

AWID default All zeros; AWLEN All zeros, Length 1; AWSIZE Data bus width; AWBURST 0b01 INCR; AWLOCK All zeros Normal access; AWCACHE 0b0000; AWQOS 0b0000; WSTRB All ones; BRESP 0b00 OKAY (slave-side default). ARID, ARLEN, ARSIZE, ARBURST, ARLOCK, ARCACHE, ARQOS all have the same defaults as their AW counterparts.

When a master uses the AxLOCK signals for a transaction to show that it is a locked transaction then the interconnect must ensure that only that master can access the targeted slave region, until an unlocked transaction from the same master completes. An arbiter within the interconnect must enforce this restriction.
In an AXI4 environment, any AXI3 locked transaction is converted as follows: AWLOCK[1:0] = 0b10 -> AWLOCK = 0b0; ARLOCK[1:0] = 0b10 -> ARLOCK = 0b0.
In AXI4, all Device transactions using the same ID to the same slave must be ordered with respect to each other. This ordering is not an explicit requirement of AXI3.

Transaction requests on the same channel, with the same ID and destination are guaranteed to remain in order. The ordering model does not give any ordering guarantees between transactions from different masters, read and write transactions, transactions with different IDs, transactions to different Peripheral regions, or transactions to different Memory locations.

agent_value.spec_section: A6.2 Memory locations and Peripheral regions
agent_value.quote: A Memory location has all of the following properties: a read of a byte returns the last value written; write updates value; accesses have no side-effects on other Memory locations; size = single-copy atomicity size. A Peripheral region has all of: read does not necessarily return last value written; write does not necessarily update; accesses may have side-effects on other addresses within the region; size is IMPLEMENTATION DEFINED but must be contained within a single slave component.
